dataList.content: A Pawnshop

You see, it takes more than a run of bad luck and an empty wallet for someone to step into a pawnshop willingly. People are more inclined to endure the shabby, wretched racket of "getting by" than one might think. ... Until even their faint hopes for tomorrow desert them.
That's when they start crowding this dingy place, ready to part with the most precious pieces of their past.

On the display, you see a prosthetic right arm adorned with raised patterns, a train ticket to who-knows-where, and a rusted fountain pen that still looks as though it might fetch something.

You linger awkwardly, but the owner has clearly seen your sort a thousand times before. Without so much as looking up, they ask, "So, what do you have?"

You rummage through your pockets and...
Lay everything I have on the counter.
Offer only the least valuable thing I own.
Turn away from that appraising gaze and make a run for it.
Stand-in Exam

You are approached by a group gathered in an alley.

"You know, for tomorrow's practical exam... well, let's say they're not too particular about checking faces. 

It doesn't take long for you to work out what they're getting at.

"And my children are still so young. They just don't have much experience."

Someone beside them picks up the thread.

"But we've heard that if they earn all their certifications by the end of this month, they'll get extra points at next month's job interviews..."

Nobody mentions what the exam is actually for. Still, perhaps people like you might be able to give these people a small leg up on their way to achieving that dream of Nest life?
Send one Sinner. They don't look happy about it, but someone has to do it.
Draw lots and send two Sinners. That should give as many applicants as possible a chance to pass.
Stay out of it. Moving into a Nest is never going to be that easy.
An Overcrowded Playground

A moving truck loaded with someone's belongings squeezes into the narrow alley. Every child in the playground turns to look, but what a shame—not a single face lights up in welcome.

"But the playground's already full. 8 on the red swings, 5 on the green ones, 10 on the slide, 4.5 on the steps, and 10 on the seesaw."

The child who seems to be in charge counts the kids off, each syllable crisp and clear.

"Where are we even supposed to put the new kid?"
On the sand. It's the only place left for a latecomer.
On the red swings. Maybe there's room to squeeze in just one more?
Stay out of the headcount. Turn my back on the children and walk away.
Counterfeit Business Card

"You could be anyone. Even someone you never dared to dream of being."

The owner runs through the pitch with the ease of someone who's heard more than a few hard-luck stories.
For all the grand promises, though, they're holding nothing more than a few business cards.

"On this little piece of paper, at least, you're a team leader at K Corp. Or the director of a Grade 5 Fixer Office, if you prefer. Mind you, if the inspectors come knocking, this is a fruit shop, and all you've bought today is a nice, ripe apple."

With one of those artfully forged cards in hand... you could be anyone.
Try being someone else. Anyone will do, so long as it isn't who I am now.
Become a new hire at a Wing. That should leave plenty of people green with envy.
Stick with who I am. This life isn't so bad, all things considered.
A Hill of Rags

Between the crowded market stalls, a hill rises into your view. You take a closer look, soon realizing that it contains layers upon layers of clothing; perhaps the whole town's laundry has found its way into the pile? It's their lives and experiences worn thin, creased, crumpled, filthy, reeking.

Maybe it wouldn't hurt to take an outfit along, something to set aside for later. Our own clothes will find their way down to the foot of this hill one day...
Take a suit. Another rinse and a good ironing might make it look presentable enough.
Take the hide of... something. Wandering these streets, there may come a time when looking human isn't such a good idea.
Take nothing. What I'm wearing will do.
An Empty Bus Stop

You find yourself at a bus stop, not a soul to be seen.
A bus from nowhere pulls up in front of you; you have no idea where it's going.
As though returning the favor for all the time you've spent waiting, it waits patiently without so much as a honk.
But it won't wait for you forever.
Even after night has fallen, the Backstreets have another night in store, after all...
You'd better decide how you're getting home, and quickly.
Get on the bus.
Head off on foot, following the way I remember.
Let the bus go and stay at the stop. But will there even be another one?
White Nights

You see a brilliant pillar of light shooting up to the sky, its rays cutting through the gaps between the tightly packed buildings. Your whole world lights up, as though night itself has ceased to exist.
One by one, the people of the Backstreets lift their heads toward the sky.
Beneath that gentle, warm light, you...
Look up at the sky with everyone else.
Look down at the light scattering across the uneven pavement.
Just squeeze my eyes shut.
A Wall Full of Rumors

From petty errands to expeditions and contract killings, there's never a shortage of work for a Fixer, is there?
The pay for each job looks fair enough. On paper, at least.
But which will you take, and which will you turn a blind eye to? The choice is yours.
Urban Myth. Take on the sort of job that's familiar enough.
Follow a Canard that might turn a profit.
Urban Legend. Take on a job that offers a hefty payout.
Take none of the contracts.
Familiar Yet Unknown Alleyways

The labyrinthine network of alleyways winds on, one turn after another. These Backstreets resemble every alley you can remember, yet somehow none of them feel familiar. You keep walking, turn after turn, but there's no end in sight. Then, all at once, a sudden realization comes to you: this odd feeling that's been tugging at your attention is...
The darkness closing in around me. Better take out my PDA and check the time.

3:13 AM.
When the "Night" falls on the Backstreets, they come.
Come sunrise, there won't be a trace of anything left behind.
Music drifting from somewhere. It's got a catchy beat.

Clinking chains. Boisterous guffaw. Right, the Middle never forgets. Once you're in their bad books, you'll be on the run for the rest of your life... only to inevitably find them waiting at the mouth of some alleyway.
The sound of something barking...
One starts barking, and soon every alley is barking in tandem. The four-legged things crawl on these streets, howling into the air without even figuring out what they are meant to guard.
Nothing worth stopping for. Keep walking.
I decide to keep moving. What I'm waiting for might not be in this alley at all.
Nothing that matters. I don't want to care about anything anymore.
Whatever it is, I have no desire to find out. Soon, those stirrings will die away. Then something else will come along to fill the silence.
Dark Cloud

You wander into the cul-de-sac of some labyrinthine network of alleyways.
This Backstreets you've stepped into is unlike any street you've walked before; it is at once unfamiliar and disinterested.
With nothing but your memories as drawing paper, you begin sketching the life in this Backstreets, caring little for what is true or false, what is weak or powerful...
As the disinterest of the streets turns into a specific, unwelcome interest, black clouds stretching from your thoughts cast shadows just as long and dark over the alleyway.
Cut through the cumulus.

Ten Blades of the East. Blade Fiend. Ashura.
Each warrior who held one of those titles has brought me again and again before the gates of hell, searing themselves deep into my memories with agony as their brand.

Here awaits...
Flee from the cumulus.
There is no need to step into the crafted world.
